speaking_script:
**[0–2 min — Hook]**
A family has a recurring Friday problem. Everyone arrives late. One adult blames traffic; children blame hunger; another voice says, “This is our karma; nothing can change.” Devices stay on; no one prepared food; irritation spreads before kīrtana. Hold the picture without shaming anyone in the room. Ask: Which lenses are missing — action, choice, modes, false promise, or shelter?

**[2–6 min — Review chain map]**
Walk the five verses as a single family practice, not five new lectures:
- BG 3.9 — Is the action shaped toward Viṣṇu or toward binding self-interest?
- BG 18.63 — Have we deliberated, or are we reacting on autopilot / fatalism?
- BG 2.22 — Do we remember the soul’s journey so consequences matter without despair?
- BG 14.5 — What mode-weather is coloring the room (rush, fog, clarity)?
- BG 7.14 — What shelter crosses the false promise of “nothing can change” or “willpower alone”?
State clearly: tonight is synthesis. Do not invent new doctrine. Do not dump Cycle 3 ontology.

**[6–10 min — Five-lens method]**
Teach the five lenses on the board: (1) Action, (2) Choice, (3) Modes/conditioning, (4) False promise, (5) Devotional shelter. A complete family response names all five. Missing a lens creates distortion: blame-only, fatalism, mode-label insults, or white-knuckle force without shelter.

**[10–14 min — Analogy + scriptural arc]**
Use the “five camera angles on one scene” analogy with its limit. Briefly paraphrase the review meanings already taught earlier in Cycle 2. No invented dialogue. No full purport dumps.

**[14–18 min — Constructed case]**
Read Constructed Case 1 (Friday rush / fatalism). Ask the room to fill each lens in one short phrase. Affirm effort; correct fatalism kindly: BG 18.63 invites deliberation and choice under guidance.

**[18–20 min — Lab preview + transition]**
Preview Five-Lens Family Case Lab. At 2:28: parents stay in parent circle; younger and older tracks; reunite at 3:10. Parents remain onsite.
core_explanation: Cycle 2 taught action and sacrifice (BG 3.9), responsible choice after hearing (BG 18.63), the soul’s changing of bodies (BG 2.22), bondage by the three modes (BG 14.5), and crossing māyā by surrender (BG 7.14). Integration Night weaves these into one coherent family practice: analyze without blame, choose without fatalism, and pair boundaries with shelter. This is synthesis — not ranking families and not opening a new doctrine track.

devotional:
**Integration as responsible choice (classroom paraphrase of the Gītā’s closing invitation in BG 18.63):** After receiving knowledge, the devotee is not frozen by fate-language nor licensed for ego whim — deliberation and guided choice remain part of bhakti culture.
**Use:** Centers Integration Night without new doctrine.
**Limitation:** Point learners to the five VedaBase URLs for personal study; invent no lecture anecdotes about cohort families.

speaking_script:
**[0–2 min — Hook]**
Two children argue “Mine!” over toys. A sincere adult hears two confident speakers disagree online about a “must-do” spiritual rule. Which door do we use: celebrity charisma, fear, or ask–serve–verify with śāstra?

speaking_script:
**[0–2 min — Hook]**
A family thinks “we already do kindness” and wonders why bhakti needs nine processes. Kindness is good; Prahlāda’s answer aims devotion offered to Viṣṇu.

**[2–7 min — Both verses]**
Read/display ŚB 7.5.23 and 7.5.24. Name all nine. Emphasize iti puṁsārpitā viṣṇau — offered to Viṣṇu — as what makes it topmost learning.

**[7–12 min — Map without panic]**
Show that families may be strong in śravaṇa/kīrtana and thin elsewhere. One underused process can be added once — not all nine mastery.

**[12–16 min — Analogy]**
Nine doors to one home — object is Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa.

**[16–18 min — Case]**
Generic virtue without object — correct.

**[18–20 min — Lab preview]**
Stations rotation; tracks at 2:28.
core_explanation: Prahlāda lists nine processes of pure bhakti centered on Viṣṇu. Verse 24’s iti puṁsārpitā teaches that when this bhakti is offered to Viṣṇu, it is the highest learning. KUTUMBA families continue a core practice and gently add one underused process — never generic virtue with the Lord removed, and never panic mastery of all nine at once.
